# Loop Engineering Crash Course

> A free, open-source curriculum for loop engineering: designing control systems that keep
> AI coding agents working toward a goal over time. 6 parts, 14 steps, 20 starter kits,
> graded labs, and a Loop Ready certification. MIT licensed.

Loop engineering is the practice of designing the system that prompts an AI agent — its
trigger, instructions, guardrails, verification, state, and logging — rather than prompting
it by hand. Every production loop declares six parts: a heartbeat (when it runs), a body
(what it can do), a spine (what it remembers), a stopping condition (when it's done), a
checker (who verifies), and a human gate (where a person decides).

Every page below is published on this domain. The source markdown lives at
https://github.com/ayeshakhalid192007-dev/LoopEngineering-CrashCourse.

## Course

- [Start Here — the 60-second router](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/start-here/): You are one honest answer away from knowing exactly where to begin. No account, no sign-up, no placement test — just read the four questions below and…
- [Prerequisites](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/prerequisites/): What to have in place before the first loop runs: a working agentic coding setup, the spec-driven habits the course assumes, and a primer on agentic coding itself. Skip whichever you already know.
- [Foundations](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/foundations/): The vocabulary and mental models the rest of the course leans on. Read these once and the six parts of a loop stop being jargon.
- [Part 1 · The Shift](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/parts/the-shift/): From prompting to looping: what actually changes, which layer you're standing in, and the six-part anatomy every loop shares. This part is pure mental…
- [Part 2 · The Heartbeat](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/parts/heartbeat/): Four ways a loop decides when to beat — from a timer you can watch tick, to the world itself reaching over and pulling the trigger. Read this part as a…
- [Part 3 · The Body](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/parts/the-body/): What a beat may do and touch — and how to keep many hands from colliding: isolation, taught moves, hands on the world, and the split that keeps work…
- [Part 4 · The Spine](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/parts/the-spine/): One step, one organ, one unbending rule: the model forgets, so the files have to remember. This is the briefest part of the whole course — and the one…
- [Part 5 · A Complete Loop, Twice](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/parts/complete-loop/): The capstone of the build track: every organ from Parts 1–4 wired together into one production loop — and then wired together again in a second tool,…
- [Part 6 · Human Control](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/parts/human-control/): The course ends exactly where accountability lives: with you. Four pages on the one job that can't be handed off — paying for, verifying, and…

## Build

- [Loop Patterns](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/patterns/): Named, reusable loop designs. Each pattern states what the loop watches, what it may do, how it verifies its own output, and where a human stays in the…
- [starters/ — install-and-run loop kits](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/starters/): A loop is a handful of small files: a definition, a spine, a budget, a constitution, a skill, and a checker. This folder hands you those files…
- [Projects](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/projects/): Eleven graded labs. Each one builds a working loop end to end, then breaks it on purpose so you learn what failure looks like before production teaches…
- [Methods](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/methods/): The reusable procedures — how to choose a pattern, how to check a loop design before you run it, and how to scaffold a new loop from a template. These are the pages you come back to, not the ones you read once.
- [Operating](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/operating/): Running loops in anger: the failure modes, the anti-patterns, what observability a loop needs, how to recover one that has gone wrong, and how to keep an infinite loop from being infinite.
- [Advanced](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/advanced/): What comes after your first working loop: making it better on purpose, running several at once, and keeping a fleet of them accountable.

## Reference

- [Assessments](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/certification/): How you find out whether you actually learned this. Graded against a written rubric, not against a feeling.
- [Appendix](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/appendix/): Reference material — per-tool cheatsheets for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Windsurf and Grok, plus the routines reference.
- [Course Contents — read in folder order](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/curriculum/): New here? Open 00-start-here/ first — the 60-second router that drops you onto a track. The folders below are numbered in reading order, so the listing…

- [Core Concepts](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/foundations/concepts/): Intent debt, comprehension debt, and the harness-vs-loop distinction — the three ideas that explain most loop failures before they happen.
- [Primitives](https://ayeshakhalid192007-dev.github.io/loop-lab/foundations/primitives/): The raw materials every loop is assembled from — and what each one is for once the goal is autonomy instead of assistance.
